title: 5 year user leaving, can’t recommend
body:
Was a loyal user of Forest for 5 years, I paid for the app and loved it for 4 of those years

The app took a new direction around a year ago, it moved from a one-time fee to a freemium model and this was the beginning of the slop

The app moved from incredibly stable to receiving regular forced updates that introduced bugs. The team introduced more trees along with daily login events and timed events. This completely defeats the point of getting off your phone and focusing. When your focus app needs you to log in daily and rewards you with cosmetics, it is no longer a focus app, it’s part of the problem.

Under the most recent update they removed the ability to configure “favourites” which were easy to pick combinations of tags and trees, completely gutting my use of the app and violating their promise of retaining pro features that users paid for.

Do not trust this company, do not download this app. It will demand your attention and focus on your screen, it will not help you focus on other things. It’s a shame as it was a great app for many years.

They should’ve left the app as it was and paid for the marketing of a new app, but instead they chose to predate their own user base in lieu of taking the risk of launching a new app.

title: Recent App Update
body:
I’ve been using Forest for almost a decade because I’ve always loved how simple and minimal it was. Unfortunately, this latest update has made the user journey much longer for no real gain.

The timer is a good example: before, I could simply use the time on the screen itself and start. Now I have to click Time → select the timer → click focus again.

The finish is even more frustrating. I don’t want to claim coins every time. Previously, I could simply hit back and start the next session. Now I have to click Claim Coins → hit continue-> go back to Home → select the timer/tree again → decide the time-> hit focus. The Restart button on iPhone also no longer works without claiming the coins first.

On top of that, favourites have disappeared, so I have to manually select my usual timer and tree every time.

This isn’t about getting used to change, I’ve been happy with previous updates. It’s that this update has added several unnecessary clicks to something that used to be incredibly quick and seamless.

I’m sure other long-term users feel the same way. I really hope you’ll consider reverting these changes, or at least provide a workaround. I’d love to keep using Forest, but this extra friction is making me consider alternatives.

title: Terrible now they’ve made it free
body: This used to be a really phenomenal app and perfect for studying as an undergraduate student. It used to be really helpful for focusing and also helped with motivation and planting more trees. However now they’re clearly trying to squeeze even more money out of users in the pursuit of further profit. I paid for this app rather than the many others that are free, because it explicitly did not have ads and all features would be accessible once you purchase it. Now however, they’ve shifted to making it free but with yet another subscription service meant to harass people into buying it. There’s now ads that make the app buggy, and constant efforts to try and get you to spend more on it. This is extremely frustrating and dishonest particularly to those of us who have paid to download it. At first they made us into a “pro” service with no ads but now they’ve introduced a “plus” group and have started to spam the pro group with ads to get them to purchase the plus and subscribe to yet another racketeering scheme. Absolutely disgraceful behaviour. Do not waste your money on this and go download one of the many other productivity apps where at the very least you know what you’re paying for.

title: Best app ever!
body: I got this app for university since I would spend a lot of time on my phone and I didn’t know how long I was doing work for. So I bought this app on my iPad, and honestly it’s amazing! I love plants so it’s very motivating to unlock plants through challenges and such, I especially love the plants changing for seasons or holidays. I have planted my first tree, I have had the app since November.. I love it so much that I also bought it on my phone since it’s Samsung so it syncs better. I use it all of the time and now I can estimate how long a task would take me based off my previous forest times and tags as well. I have never been more productive for so long, I usually lose interest and  motivation after 2-3 months, but still going strong 💪💪 Summary, I love it so much. I definitely recommend to any students or anyone wanting to track how they are using their time or have any personal projects they just want to track. Forest is my 2024 app of the year!

title: Great, but could also have…
body:
I think the app is great! I especially love the customisation for allowing certain apps without killing your tree since I am an iPad user and I no longer have an iPhone.

Things I would improve / want to see: 
Missing out on event trees is a big shame in my opinion and seeing as the app is already a payed app and these trees were free during their event, I would like to see the opportunity to earn these trees for free. Maybe having a certain amount of study hours (these can be high like 500+) you can earn a tree. Or maybe at a certain accumulated hours you can earn the currency required to pay for these trees. Either way some way to earn it so everyone has the chance to unlock trees that were once free. Since most students use this app and would like to use the adorable event trees. The option to pay can still be available for those who are impatient.

Compared with other focus apps, I think a section with a To-do list would help me increase my productivity. It would be nice to have everything I need to do all on one app. It would be great if it was customisable like setting a certain task to be complete at a certain time in a certain time frame (Eg 1hr) and the to-do list can be colour coded to group specific types of tasks.

title: A very good app
body:
This is an incredible app - its helping me track my productivity and helps me to focus on a specific task. I really like how the graphs have shown me where I lull (typically 2-3pm ish) during the day, and how I can label different times to different jobs, so I know how I’m splitting my time. The graphics are very cute, I like all the little trees, and I like that I can also put some of my coins towards plant real trees, not just virtual ones (there is currently a max of 5 ‘real’ trees - I hope it increases soon!) . I highly recommend this app.

If I had to change one thing, I’d like an update to the design variances in some of the flowers. For quite a few different tree species, the icon varies slightly at different time points (e.g looks slightly bigger at 1 hour vs 30 mins), but the flowers don’t get the same love! It would be really nice for the flowers to look bigger when you’ve spent longer focusing.

title: Stop sending spam notifications
body:
This is a productivity tool, it should send notifications related to its functioning, and nothing else. I ally couldn’t care less if it’s Forest’s birthday, and I certainly don’t need to be reminded about it daily.

I’m now in a position of having to choose whether to disable notifications and render the app unusable, or leave them enabled and allow the app to continue to bug me about unimportant nonsense I’ve always repeatedly dismissed. A choice I should not need to make in an app I have paid to use. 

I even read the news article in an attempt to shut it up. But it’s not relevant to me as someone who doesn’t use social media, and it didn’t stop the incessant nagging anyway. 

Invest your time and energy into making the app better and easier to use, not into making a spamming tool.

title: A kinder way to focus than barring access to apps
body:
Have to say, I tried Opal as an add on to the iOS screen time functionality.  It just made me feel bad about myself.  Forest approaches the problem of focus and distraction from the other direction - one of positivity.

It’s got the functionality I need to encourage focus, the carrot, not the stick.  I just want to snap stick, personally.  I particularly like the timer visible on the Lock Screen - this is an instant reminder on pickup of the phone that I have chosen to focus for this period of time. 

That distinction is crucial, and what sets it apart from iOS screen time or others like Opal.

title: Unsatisfied with customer feedback, dismissive response.
body: I have had the app forest for over 2 years now and until now have had no complaints. However, the problems started a few days ago when I made a new account for a 'fresh start' for the next set of exams I have this year. There is a section in the app where you can submit a referral code when someone has referred the app to you and you receive an award. I submitted the code from my previous account, unaware that this was a violation of forest's rules and now have been banned from submitting another referral code in the future. I reached out to the customer service chat about this and I received a standardised, unhelpful, not personalised response that did not resolve the problem at hand and felt dismissive. This is not clearly listed on the referral code page and should be further emphasised to users considering a 'second chance' is not given. It's inexcusable to treat your customers this way. I have suggested this app to many friends and family and been a user for a long time!! Surely you should take responsibility for this 'violation' which was not made clear? Surely you don't expect your customers to have the Terms and conditions of Forest memorised? I thought the developers of the app made Forest to aid studying and productivity, not ridiculously punish their users.  Extremely unsatisfied. Please resolve this matter.

title: Could be MUCH better
body:
Trying to connect to my friends (who i have in my contacts) has been near impossible… I sent an invite code which they used and they’re still not even appearing on my forest friends list?? 

How is this not automatic? 

WARNING FOR NEW USERS

You will have to actually send an email to your friends so that they’ll even appear on the app for a group study session together. Don’t bother, it’s a Nightmare. 

Students, you’re better off doing a silent zoom call with your friends then trying to study with them on this app. The people behind the chat feedback function are taking a snooze until tomorrow (according to the app) for the day.. so good luck reporting any further issues.

Save your time, money and energy and go elsewhere

body: I struggle to focus without some kind of external motivation and this app has been really useful so far. When I want to give up I picture the withered little trees and it helps me to hang in and refocus for the remainder of the 25 minutes slots. I love seeing my little healthy forest at the end of the day. A big motivator for me is the idea that I can plant a real tree once I’ve accumulated enough coins, so this really pushes me to focus more than I perhaps would in an average day. I am getting a lot done and enjoying the motivation, so win-win!
author: shezLC

title: Lovely app, works great on iPhone but needs work on iPad
body: I truly adore this app. Growing (or killing) your little digital trees and seeing your forest expand is genuinely motivating and really does keep you from going on your phone and getting distracted. The price is more than fair, and what really drew me to this app over some of the similar competition is the fact that it has a proper iPad version, which none of the others do. The layout and art style is nice, and being able to view your daily/ weekly/ monthly and yearly forest is both pretty and motivating - widgets can currently only display your ‘daily’ forest efforts and I would love to see at least weekly and monthly widgets in the future, especially on iPad where you have additional screen space to enjoy your forest. The reason I can only give 4 stars in the app’s current state is because the [iPad version] widgets simply do not work. Instead, the widgets display as completely blank white squares/ rectangles, which is a shame because the widgets are actually really good on the iPhone. After multiple reinstalls of the app, I did manage to get the iPad widgets working for a day or two and they seemed nice. There was definitely some scaling issues when displaying the forest tile though, which looked too small inside the widget once you had something in your forest for that day, and if you didn’t, then the empty forest tile appeared larger and pixelated. Sadly, the widget has since stopped working altogether and I can’t get it working again. On the plus side, the customer service seems good, and they reply fairly quickly and are friendly and understanding, so hopefully these issues will be ironed out soon. The app deserves 5 stars all day long once these bugs are sorted :)

title: A useful coping mechanism for ADHD brains 🌱🧠
body: I have tried so many different tools to help keep me on track when my neurodivergent brain has other plans. Forest is absolutely perfect for me because it can help me break tasks down into manageable chunks and gives me the motivation of a deadline to help keep my focus on track. I use it with the pomodoro technique, it’s far better than a noisy alarm or bell and won’t distract my colleagues. The bonus is you get the visual aid and reward of having some cute trees (or if you are spooky like me, pumpkins and ghost mushrooms). When it adds up you can enjoy the sense of achievement which I find super encouraging, particularly on days where I am feeling overwhelmed and fighting invisible barriers. I like that you can tag your focus sprints into categories too. Thank you for this amazing tool. ❤️🌱

CONS: 
• Sometimes the phone app can be a little messy with its lay out
• the price for the trees you get can probably deter people from progressing and sticking with the app, I suggest making some of them cheaper so they get hooked on the progression of the forest more easily :)
• The extension for chrome could use a little more work and give the same level of functionality as the app on your phone (which I would use primarily) but the

IN SHORT: 
The app is great for productivity but needs minor changes to make it better, I would give it 4.5/5 stars and would try it anyway. Don’t let the price put you off 😊

title: Amazing except for 2 things
body:
This is a really good app for those of us with bad habits of picking up our phones and mindlessly and needlessly distracting ourselves. It feels great to see all the trees you've planted through your focused time. 

Two things that would really make the app even better:
1) it's too difficult to get coins. When new plants/trees can cost over 1000 coins (even 2000 coons) and you get less than half a coin per minute of focus time, it can feel way too difficult to unlock new plants for your forest. 
1) emergency button of some sort - it would be great to have an option to have some kind of emergency "need to exit the app for this one tiny thing without killing my trees" button, even better if it's a kind of timed feature, like you have 1 minute to do whatever you need to do before your plant dies. I started planting some trees for a 2 hour session before realising that I needed to look at my notes app because I couldn't remember a password. I had no choice but to leave the app because I needed the password otherwise I couldn't connect to wifi and get on with my work. Unfortunately it cost me 4 dead trees. It was disappointing because I did actually focus for the time period, but just needed to pop out of the app quickly to get this password.

title: Good
body:
Pluses
- very nice aesthetic 
- polished
- building a forests is cool 
- very reasonable price  (and not a subscription!)

Negatives 
- doesn't support swiping, so you need to click a button to go back and plant a new tree. Fee is clunky and takes away your ‘flow’
- tags can't be deleted/marked complete and are awkward to select while planting trees, so if you want to track time against loads of small tasks (for example discrete work tasks ) the ui will get in your way

In summary, it's good for what it is. I'd recommend it if you don't have a ton of tasks you want to track.

title: AMAZING!!!
body: This app is INCREDIBLE, and totally worth every penny!!! I often get distracted by my phone when I’m trying to study, but this app genuinely works. You wouldn’t think that planting virtual trees would help productivity but it really does! And I love the wide range of trees you can get. It’s also really great being able to plant trees in real life, but my one problem with that is that when you plant a tree, literally nothing happens. You press a button, and then that’s it. I think it would be nice to get at least a little notification to tell you your awesome and you planted a tree, but none of that happens. I planted my first real tree yesterday, and I actually got worried that it hadn’t gone through because so little happened. But apart from that, this app is flawless, and it really makes you feel good when you don’t go on your phone.

a. If Forest app wants to penetrate the UK college student market, what are some opportunities or strategies that we can use to reach these target audiences?” Literally gathering the work for free. It is especially upsetting because the actual app is actually brilliant. I’m beyond shocked at the company’s ethics.

title: Download NOW!! to beat procrastination and enhance productivity.
body: I rarely leave feedbacks for Apps, idk why but that's besides the point. After facing a lull in productivity and motivation with the lockdown and being back at home I decided to check this app out and silently wished for it to be worth it since I was paying to try it out but im very pleased to share with you all that it has indeed been worth it. It's great to use when tracking your production levels, and comparing it against previous moments really serves as a motivation and encouragement booster. I love the new stopwatch feature which actually suits me when I feel motivated to work but don’t want to risk a withered tree should I lose concentration but also the countdown feature is perfect for when I need a little push and tell myself “just do an hour” I kinda wish organisations like schools can purchase this and use it to facilitate motivation in times like this. Also it would great if there was a section where you could input a target for example if your target was to study for 5 hours on that day. But there app is constantly updating and improving and I can't wait to see what they come up with next, I only wish that I found this app earlier!! Would have planted so many real life trees!! ( yes you can do that!!)

title: awesome app, great for revision
body: this is one of my go-to apps for studying and revision. I know you have to pay for the app, but it is well worth it, considering many     « free » revision apps claim they’re free and then bug you into a costly subscription. I love the system, it’s beautiful and simple and there’s something really satisfying about growing your forest; it feels like a reward for studying. The app also comes with study music and ambiance which you can turn on or off. Another thing I love is collecting trees and new sounds with the coins you get after a study session. One thing i might say though is that currently im using on an ipad and a landscape mode hasn’t been developed yet, which is has caused me some annoyance. Hopefully this gets resolved in future updates, but apart from that, great app, and definitely worth buying.

title: Love it
body: This app helps me to maintain focus on what I am currently working on. I often get distracted by notifications or simply going to check the time and then begin searching through social apps and before I know it half an hour to an hour has passed and I haven’t completed what I had set out to. The timer on this app helps me to avoid looking or using my phone for that set amount of time. I use it like a game and challenge myself so see how long I can go without disengaging. It’s also nice to see what a lovely little forest you can create after focusing for so much time. It’s really simple to use and there isn’t too much going on which I’ve found with over free apps there’s a lot more you can do and I just feel that adds to more distraction. Worth the small price of £1.99.

title: Amazing but a few suggestion for improvement
body:
Forest is incredible and really motivating. The only few suggestions I could make is:

-there is the break button that appears after you have successfully planted a tree and have done the time. However, I keep forgetting it’s there. It would be bette rid on the actual home page where you plant the tree, if there is a break function.
- to be able to have a chat feature so when you’re organising group sessions, it will be more seamless and less hassle.
- a weekly leaderboard. When you go to your friends, you can see their daily usage. My friends and I use this as a sort of leaderboard for friendly competition and motivation (I am unsure if that is how it is meant to be used). However, I feel it would be more impactful if you can see someone’s weekly hours or even more. Maybe it could be an option if some people find that uncomfortable.

Those are my suggestions but the app is just fantastic without them anyway. Thank you for creating such a useful tool!

title: Forest Review
body:
Forest is a great app and I recommend it for everyone who wants to reduce screen time or focus for work or hobbies. It’s unique feature of planting trees really does motivate you to not pick up your phone. Personally I have got so much more work done thanks to this app. It also gives a visual representation in a pie chart and also most productive times of the day and week this helps focus down in those areas

Improvements to make 
Although forest is a great app, it does need some improvements in my opinion
- to be able to change the tag of what you are doing DURING when the timer is on (it’s annoying when you set the wrong tag for something and you can’t change it during the timer because otherwise it kills the tree)
- when a timer/tree is started, to get a notification saying when the tree will be planted eg if at 3 o clock there was a 2 hour tree planted a notification would pop up saying “tree will be planted at 5 o clock
- to be able to set the time in hours and minutes rather than in minutes (this just makes it easier because usually people work in hours and minutes rather than just minutes)
- when checking the timeline of events, to be able to update the note/tag

All in all forest is a great app and I highly recommend everyone to try it!

title: Remove audio
body:
Great idea and love that it helps with productivity. 

Just had to delete it because my AirPods Pro keep connecting to my iPhone. Why? Because forest app plays music in the background (its muted by default). 

Because of that, as soon as you pause your music or video on your laptop, it automatically connects to your iPhone.
 
If you have to do connect your AirPods back to your Mac 10-15 times a day (if not more), it gets annoying after a few days. 

Developers, give us an option where we can stop audio completely, not just muting the Audio. Thanks in advance!

title: Focusing on payments
body:
I like the app, definitely helps. What I don’t follow is this precedence by forest upon micro transactions... for example to delete my log I have to “pay 60 coins”.
Why?
This isn’t a computer game. Rather than focusing on adding actual value, you’ve focused on squeezing people for money at every opportunity. How about focusing on adding value. I’d happily pay for better features. 
I await your generic reply that “making good apps with great features needs money”. It’s always a classic to see that kind of response, almost like paying £2 for a glorified clock wasn’t good enough.

title: Should be free
body:
Why make us pay £1.99 for the app and make only two types of boring plants available? 

If it was a free app and you had to pay for additional trees I’d understand. But for £1.99 you get very little value. At least make 10 - 20 trees available at the beginning, considering the user has spent £1.99 on a very simple app, which I doubt requires much in terms of updates.

The graphics could be much more interesting as well. I’d suggest making the trees bigger on screen and make it interesting/satisfying to look at whilst the timer is on. For example if you could see some constant growth. Considering the whole app is about trees/plants the graphics aren’t good enough in my opinion.

title: Forest App or Flora App?
body:
I really like the premise of this app; I love the fact that it helps you focus, I love the little gardens you can grow and the fact that you can plant real trees is amazing! 

I will say, I definitely prefer the garden of the Forest app. I like that it’s a bit more interactive, more interesting to look at and I like that it is somewhat 3D compared to the Flora app. 

But I really don’t like the coin system for unlocking other plants. I’ve been using a similar app, Flora, for years now and know that Forest and Flora used to be in partnership, but that was terminated due to Forest’s decision to charge for the app and some in-app purchases. 

In the Flora app, you unlock new plants with focus time, and I think that’s a brilliant system! Unlocking the new plants really helped to keep me motivated and I got a little buzz every time I unlocked a new plant. 

I really think that Forest should considering removing the coin system and replacing it with the focus time unlockables. Or at the very least, make it easier to earn coins! With the cheapest new tree costing 300 coins, I’ve found it takes a long time to gain enough coins to unlock a new tree, and it gets boring very quickly having to plant the same species of tree again and again. Not to mention that all of the tree species on the cheaper end of the scale look pretty much the same, it’s hard to get any kind of colour or variety into your virtual garden! The gardens on Flora are beautiful and colourful, and I have a little smile on my face when I see all the plants I’ve “grown” in a study session!

Flora is definitely my personal presence between the two apps, and I will be going back to it. But I really hope that the developers or Forest take this as constructive criticism, and maybe even make some improvements!

title: Tried, Tested & Adored for 3 Years
body:
1.) It helps me filter out distractions. Like most of us if we are being honest, a mobile phone can be the enemy of concentration. This app prevents you from playing on your phone & incentivises you to focus & stay off it. You plant trees by achieving concentration for a set time & this builds up to a forest 🌳 ⁣
⁣
2.) It breaks my study time in to manageable chunks. A bit like the Pomodoro technique, with a countdown timer & the inability to use your phone, else your lovely little plant won’t grow 🌱 ⁣
⁣
3.) It reduces my screentime. I imagine I’m not the only person who has been horrified by their screen time reports, especially during the lockdown. The app makes me less dependent on my phone & helps me focus on work, rather than being a slave to notifications 📲 ⁣

title: Best app for actual productivity!
body:
I’ve tried so many productivity apps. Most focus on lists, but this one focuses on focus itself and complements the others perfectly. If you struggle with time management, like me, this app is highly effective. I have achieved so much in a short space of time - jobs I have procrastinated on for weeks that I never thought I could achieve in a matter of hours or a couple of days. 

If you really struggle to focus, start by setting the timer for 10-15 minutes and build up to longer periods, depending on the activity. You may find, as I do, that short bursts work better for most things but it’s also invaluable if you struggle not to check your phone during your daily fitness workout! 

I love that I can custom tag and label my activities, so that I can monitor where I am spending the most time and adjust if necessary. Plus, the coins you earn by being focused can be redeemed for the planting of real trees in a real forest! 

Be warned: challenging yourself to beat the clock becomes quite addictive! 

Righto - time to get back to my Forest!

Can’t start a session from Apple Watch. When a session is started it doesn’t allow you to view it on Apple Watch face.

What would be ideal are the following features:
1. Able to start session from Apple Watch

2. When session is active, Apple Watch takes up whole screen with the time remaining, the tree. & the name of the task at hand (to focus you back to the task) and nothing else. 

3. Able to automatically set time to be until next calendar event. This would be great at work. If I only had 13 mins til next meeting, it’d be great if it knew that automatically and set the pomodoro timer to 13 mins (or an option of 11 mins, ie automatically factoring in 2 mins transition time)

title: The Original (and BEST) tree planting focus app
body:
I have used this app for the last 4 years now! Longer than almost any other app on my phone - this thing works if you need to study, it got me through my GCSEs AND A-Levels AND my first rounds of Uni exams. 
There are many clones of this app now but this one has earned its place. I love that you earn currency for planting trees which can be used to buy new species or saved up to plant a real tree. Only criticism is that the number of real trees you can plant is capped at 5 - but trust me it will take you A LONG time to hit that. 

Can’t recommend enough if you’re anything like me and gets really motivated to study... and then literally 30 seconds later is mindlessly flicking through phone.  If you need to use you’re phone for revision there is a setting for that where you’ll only earn half coins. 

If you have exams and want good grades get this app.

body:
I downloaded this app because I saw it had a simple forest theme and I have an affinity for nature.  After reading the summary and seeing the amazing reviews I decided to give it a go.

I really feel it has helped me to focus on work, the gym and studying, as well as siding jobs around the house!

Not only does it prevent you from looking at your phone (in Deep Focus mode) but it also encourages you to stay focused so you can enjoy adding a beautiful tree to your garden!

Plus having the added benefit of actually planting trees after a certain amount of points really makes you smile as you work 👍

title: Excellent for some motivation
body:
Very good Pomodoro technique to aid study. Provides motivation to not go on your phone.
Removed a star as it seems the tree grows more prestigious upon a longer study session (e.g 60 mins, rather than 25 mins) but the whole point of the Pomodoro technique is to have short sessions with small breaks, then a large break after a few sessions (e.g. 4). I feel it would be better to have the best trees rewarded for following the Pomodoro technique closely.
I also feel that the different styles of tree are out-of-reach unless you spend money on the coins, which is a bit unfair seeing as the app is not free. A suggestion for improvement could be to reward a new tree style after a set number of minutes focused (e.g. a new style for every 500 minutes), and have the coins separately for the real-life trees.

Despite these notes for improvement - the app is helping me study - would recommend.

title: Helped with my depression
body:
This app has helped me each time I’ve slumped into a depressed phase. When I feel unmotivated but desperate to lift myself out of the fog, I set a short timer (20mins usually) and just focus on one thing until the timer runs out.

Usually I’m into the flow and will do another 20 mins straight away. Seeing the little forest grow makes me feel as though I’ve achieved something- even if that something is simply washing the dishes. 🌳

I can’t recommend this app enough, especially if you struggle with mental health issues! 

Also the new trees are always so cute and it’s lovely to be able to buy a reward with your efforts.

It really is worth every penny!!

title: Out of all the things that could get me to focus,,,
body:
This app has done more for my schoolwork and revision than anything else. The fear of losing a tree is a great motivator. 
The UI and design are both absolutely wonderful and easy-to-use. The statistics and customisable tags are great for tracking how you use your revision time and downtime. There are a range of different trees and shrubs and the relatively high prices (using ingame currency) motivate you to spend more time away from your phone with this app, and they offer nothing other than aesthetic- although you can purchase the ingame currency and do it that way. Honestly, this app is definitely worth the (very little) money, as many others have already said.

title: Ben fatta
body:
Applicazione da quel che promette. inoltre aiuti il pianeta con il tuo tempo e con le monete che guadagni.
Tuttavia non mi piace il fatto che se sei immerso nel tuo lavoro e ti dimentichi di entrare nell’applicazione, il tempo trascorso non viene premiato con monete extra. Infatti tolgo una stella per questo. 
Per il resto va bene. Si può aggiungere molte idee. Per esempio: Stay away from your phone - potrebbe essere un estensione che ti premia ogni qual volta che non usi il telefono, in questo modo non c’è l’obbligo di piantare un albero con un timer specifico, ma semplicemente entrando in questa modalità parte il cronometro è più tempo passa senza usare il telefono più alberi pianti (in automatico) o si crea automaticamente un piccolo giardino.  Insomma le idee ci sono basta mettercele. 
Creiamo un mondo migliore e lasciamolo meglio di come l’abbiamo trovato. Forzaaaaa

title: Great app for procrastinators!
body:
As a serial procrastinator, this app really helps me stay on track and stay focussed, especially when I have time pressures to complete tasks on time.

You’re still able to listen to music/podcasts (although can’t leave the app, so can only change songs via control centre and lock screen), which is a major plus for me as I love listening to podcasts at work to drown out the background noise and annoying colleagues.

Once you get started, you can’t help but get invested in your forest and I find I’m less likely to enter the Wikipedia wormhole on my computer when using this app, as I feel like I’m cheating on my forest!

Highly recommend to my fellow procrastinators out there 😊

title: Pretty impressed - improvements though.
body:
So overall I think this app is pretty good. It has certainly helped me stay off my phone whilst revising or studying by making me feel incredibly guilty for killing trees. Also, I find it personally rewarding to see my trees blossom and evolve into a small forest. 

However I feel that the app could be developed in some ways to make it more fun and appealing. 
1) Make the different trees variable prices! Earning 500 coins takes a while; how about adding some smaller bushes and trees for lower prices, such as 150 and 250. 
2) I think once you get past a certain stage, it would be cool to see the landscape evolve around the forest. eg add a small stream that can also grow, or some hills or mountains possibly. It would be so cute! Also, I personally would be more motivated to use the app if I could expand on my town with rewards gained from hard work. 
3) possibly add wildlife? Such as chicks that hatch over time of squirrels or something. 

All in all - great app, definitely helps with focus. Good for feeling rewarded after and boosting productivity!

title: Silly but wow does it work!
body:
When I got told by a friend to use this I was skeptical at first. 
- Friend 'bro get this app, the less distracted you get the more your plant grows' 
- Me 'Maaannn miss me with that Captain Planet save the trees nonsense'

 You plant a tree and if you use your phone it dies and you have to start again. The longer you are focused the cooler your tree looks. The more sessions you have the bigger your forest. 

Needless to say it has helped me form a new habit of leaving my phone alone and getting stuff done, I used to pick my mob up every other minute! It even has message on screen to tell you to get back to work lol!

Yes you have to pay but I've made that back x1000s in lost productivity gained back.

Time is priceless.
Grow your trees, grow your work ethic

author: Giggle07

title: Gotta admit, I am addicted!
body:
I've been terrible at focussing on anything all my life. I fidget and task-switch all the time. It's very hard for me to concentrate of a single task without my mind drifting off, or being distracted by something unimportant. But this app has (pretty much!) saved me! I've been using it every day for a week, and it's really great. The psychological trick it plays on me is really startling — the 'tree' you grow will 'die' if you cancel the timer, or leave the app, and, despite how stupid it sounds, that alone makes me focus, preventing me from giving up. Guess I have a weak mind, haha. At any rate, I really like this app.

I do have some suggestions, however: to request nicer/more fluid animations for the growing trees; better notifications/sounds for when your timer has expired; some optimisation, for the app does seem to drain the battery on my iPhone faster than you'd expect. There’s also no update to take into account the “notch” on newer iPhone models. I’d also very much prefer an option to grow full-sized trees for shorter time periods. Make it fully customisable! Having to set a two hour work session to grow a full-sized tree (which look so much nicer than a forest of small ones!) is pretty detrimental, as concentrating for that length of time without a break is actually detrimental to learning/effective productivity. Instead, we should be able to choose what sized tree to grow, regardless of the time allotted. 

Thanks for making me more productive!

title: Tree-Mendous at improving my productivity
body: I find this app really helpful to motivate me into tackling big tasks. I tend to set the timer to 25 minutes (with a 5 minute break in between) as I find the concept of focusing for 25 minutes achievable (even if I know the task might ultimately take many days - a far more daunting prospect). Each 25 minutes results in a tree and I love growing as varied a forest as I can and comparing each day. I never want to use my phone when a tree is planted (the sight of dead trees in my virtual forest is surprisingly upsetting) and I like ending each day with a visual representation of how focused I’ve been. Plus I’m motivated to keep using the app to unlock as many species as possible.

title: Only so-so.
body: The method is sound, we all know that our phones are distracting and by locking us away from using them it can encourage good focus and help us to complete tasks while being visually rewarded with a forest. My issue is that there is unlockable content but focusing for 2 hours only earns 40 coins, the content starts off at 500 coins (20 hours of focus) but each time you use your coins the price of the next unlock increases by 100 coins. They say to utilise ‘achievements’ to get more coins but a large number of them involve connecting with friends, which is plain stupid since it’s just penalising anyone who is focusing alone, I don’t expect all my friends to pay £2 so I can connect with them! You can pay money to triple the rewards of focusing for a few days but this just makes the developers seem greedy since it’s a paid app and once the content is developed it should only require a one off purchase. Really discouraging.

title: FAULTLESS!!!
body: Forest is literally the best app I’ve come across for revision or just to keep me motivated. For a while now I’ve struggled with becoming distracted or discouraged From completing tasks or work. This app has pretty much turned this around making studying fun! So far I haven’t killed any of my trees because, although it sounds silly, the sheer guilt I feel of I stop. It allows you to do small manageable chunks but at the same time pushes you to do more by offering you the option to get a fully grown tree. Also, once you have built up your virtual coins you can spend them on: new bushes; new trees; new sounds and even plant a real tree somewhere around the world. This forces you, in a good way, to keep going as you want to unlock all the cool, new things and build your forest. You can even create a forest with friends and build it together which can be extremely motivating because you almost don’t want to let the team down. Overall the best app I’ve ever had and definitely worth the money!

title: Best Focus App
body: Forest has been an extremely useful tool for all of my examinations. I originally downloaded it whilst taking my GCSE’s but it also massively helped during my A-level examinations and now also my university work. In an age where it is so difficult to put down your phone and so easy to get distracted by messages and social media, Forest is the best way to focus. It also is rewarding, either by producing your own virtual forest or helping to contribute to growing real life trees. I recommend Forest to anyone who needs a motivation to stay off their phone and actually focus on their task at hand.

title: Such a sweet lil’ app
body:
The price of the app is worth it and (being a broke student) helps motivate you to actually use it. 
It sounds silly but you become attached to the little trees you grow.  I love physically seeing my productivity (or lack of) and it motivates me to stay on top of my endless revision. In the rapidly growing virtual world we live in, it’s nice to have a little place of calm that gives you a break from the internet. There’s also another “mode” to satisfy  your competitive side which can be used when you take part in a group study session. It’s also very motivating and helpful. Big fan.

title: Brilliant for reducing screen time!
body:
I use this app for two purposes, primarily it reduces distractions while i'm studying - i have a clear time goal, a way of monitoring that time goal and the reward of a cute little tree at the end of that study session. It breaks my study time into manageable chunks and i know that if i do get a text or notification, i only have X minutes before i can check it. 
The second reason i use this app is to reduce my screen time - restrictions on apps do little to stop me hitting "ignore time limit for today" and mindlessly scrolling for sometimes hours at a time. This app is a really effective way of getting me off my phone and into the real world and at the end of the day i can see just how much time i have spent away from my phone.
Overall a brilliant app for people who struggle to focus and also great for those with a little bit of a phone addiction like me! 
The trees and plants are a really good idea and i'm waiting for the day this app lets me plant a real tree - i'm not far off now!

title: Wonderful app
body:
This is a wonderful app. I have been planting cherry trees all spring and now have a whole forest of them. Initially just used to keep focused but have started using so I don’t use phone before bed etc. The threat of a dead tree in your forest if you use your phone once you have started your tree growing is quite powerful. You earn points for trees grown and can use these to increase your tree varieties available or to plant real trees (you need quite a lot for that)
Messages and calls still come through, and you can play music.
You can link with friends. My daughter and I  compete. 
Highly recommend this simple app to anyone wanting to spend less time online. Now back to planting trees and work...

title: Brilliant for productivity, just a few suggestions!
body: Firstly, I think forest is a wonderful app, and such a brilliant idea. It allows you to stay focused and productive, and plant real life trees to help the world. Amazing! The fact that you can plant a real tree is so unique and one of the many reasons I love this app. I also like how there is such variety in the digital plants you can buy and plant, it really adds to you wanting to use the app. However, I do work on my iPad using apps and I can only use forest on my phone because I need my iPad for work. I wish there were a way to use forest and be able to grow a plant whilst using productivity apps, as it is my iPad that is both my biggest productivity source and hinderer. If there were a way to only allow productivity apps not kill your plant so that you could still use your device without procrastination whilst using forest, this would be the perfect app. Anyway, really fantastic app, good job!

title: Best app to keep you off your phone
body:
Once you start growing a tree, it is weirdly hard to let it die! I don’t even know why but provided you muster the courage to start growing a tree, the app does a really good job of keeping you off your phone. And it’s even better when you connect with friends. 

Great for short bouts of concentration and avoiding procrastination when studying. My friends and I all swore by this app while working for GCSEs. The only time I ever properly revised was when I was growing my trees. Only complaint is that the trees are so expensive and get more expensive as you buy them so you have to spend so much time off your phone to afford the trees, but I guess it’s an even better incentive.

title: Worth spending the £2 on!
body:
Brilliant app and really helps you track how much time you are revising!
It comes with a rain sound which is really good when you need to concentrate so don’t want to listen to songs. You can also listen to spotify at the same time as long as you put it on before you start the timer on the app.
I just think that you should earn more coins for the amount of work you do because it takes forever to buy a different species of tree and you can lose motivation like that and it kind of seems like ‘oh this half an hour isn’t worth doing’. 
Also kind of annoying that if you have to work with phone mode on you only get half the coins when sometimes you have to use different apps for your work.
Overall would highly recommend!

title: Forest helped me write an essay in one day!
body: I’m so glad I downloaded this app, forest is literally pulling me through the final weeks of my last year of university. By using the app and employing the pomodoro technique, I was able to complete a 2000 word essay in one day (though I wouldn’t recommend this!). Aesthetically, the app is beautifully minimalistic. The goal to get to 2500 coins to be able to plant a real tree is extremely motivating, too. Looking at my growing forest at the end of the day is also extremely gratifying and I so wish I found this app sooner as I’m almost about to graduate. Even so, I’ll be sure to continue using forest for uses other than studying, such as to take breaks from social media. The £1.99 price tag is so worth it!

title: Changed the Revision Game!
body: Although I’m typically pretty motivated, sometimes I’d only half put effort into my revision and use Instagram and snapchat whilst “revising”..... this was not revision!!! After downloading forest, I’m revising more efficiently and spending longer revising because I love seeing my little forest grow! I compete with my friends and I like collecting the different tree types, even at a level it makes my revision a little bit more fun. There’s just something so rewarding about growing a tree, I guess it lets you see your efforts straight away! I know it costs money but it has totally transformed my revision and mindset about social media - now when I’m relaxing and chilling out I actually feel relaxed because I know I’ve accomplished something worthwhile. It also makes me feel guilty about not revising which encourages me to to revisse so it a win win!!! Couldn’t recommend any more!! Absolutely love it :)

title: Worry about less, use Forest
body: In a day and age where people are too often emersed in the internet and social media platforms, we are often left feeling overwhelmed and distracted from completing those simple yet necessary tasks in our schedules. Forest encourages concentration in a very simple way; by giving us a chance to reduce our screen-time while simultaneously encouraging the promotion of Forestation activists and projects in Africa, you feel a sense of community and productiveness when using Forest. In turn, we become aware that motivation and productivity are in fact two very 'do-able' concepts, and it is thanks to Forest that I now feel more in tune with myself, my productivity and my environmental footprint. Thanks Forest!

title: Brilliant
body: I’ve used Forest for over three years now and I’ve loved it! I bought it in my first year of uni and it’s really helped me structure my day and actually take the time to focus on my tasks almost every single day. It gives you so much data and is definitely great value for money. I love the “plant a tree in real life” feature but my only issue is that for people who use it a lot it’s very easy to max out how many trees you can plant in real life and also to buy all of the trees, bushes and sounds in the store with your coins. I’m at a point now where I’m just accumulating coins and not having anything to do with them and it diminishes the feeling of reward slightly. I think it would be great if there could be another way to spend coins to add to the feeling of reward. Overall though I love this app and I would definitely recommend it to students and also just people who want to focus their time and spend time away from their phones.
author: CupofTee

title: Very useful, easy to use and cute!
body: I’ve only been using this app a few days and it has helped me massively already. The app is super easy to use, with a very simple menu and everything is clearly labelled. I particularly love the feature that shows all the trees you’ve grown for the day, month or even year as a ‘forest’ with various stats and information about how productive you’ve been. I also really like the fact that there are lots of (very cute) different types of tree and that they can be obtained through regular use of the app rather than with in-app purchases like other apps do. You can also listen to music with the app open as long as you don’t switch apps to switch songs. The only thing that would make me love this app even more is if there were options for slightly longer and shorter growing times. Overall would highly recommend!

title: Very useful little app
body:
This app was recommended to me as a tool to help me focus on my work, as I get distracted easily. The gamification of focus tools seems to be a common thing, and in the case of Forest, I find it (personally) works really well. I’m incentivised to focus because doing so will earn me coins which I can then spend on unlocking different species of plant. 

The achievement system is/was my biggest motivator in actuality, and I would encourage the developers to include more of these - perhaps even weekly ones where you’re challenged to clock in X number of minutes for the week. Additionally, I think that the rewards for the achievements are slightly off balance as they currently stand; 30 days worth of time is a considerable amount but the payout for achieving it proportionally doesn’t seem correct in the context of the other time based achievements. 

I like that fact that unlocking the plants is solely on the effort of the user - you can pay for a multiplier in coins for a period of time, but there is nothing to give you coins directly, you have to earn them yourself. 

All in all I would definitely recommend this app.

With every session that you do with forest you earn coins which you can use to by background noise, more tree varieties and even your own real life tree which is planted somewhere in the world!

title: Couldn’t recommend this enough.
body:
As someone with ADHD, focusing for extended periods of time can prove a daunting task. Sitting down to study in the first place is challenging however staying committed to a ‘focus session’ can prove difficult for anyone. 

Forest really has solved both these issues for me. 

The nice layout of the app, coupled with the quaint feel of growing your own garden actually gives a nice incentive to sit down and make progress on whatever it is you choose to focus on. By locking the user out of the phone as well as holding you accountable for the growth of a tree serves as a nice way of keeping you committed. Without the app, I would often find it too easy to quit 5-10 minutes earlier than planned which, when done every study session, quickly adds up to hours lost daily.

Accountability partners are a great way of ensuring you stay focused and productive when going about your daily tasks and Forest is a great one at that!

Perks:
The interface is easy to use and simplistic.

The cost is justified for how much stand to gain from using the app.

The overall premise of the app is great and Forest executes it nicely.

The ‘garden’ and currency concept is a nice addition which really makes you feel content in your progress.

Downsides:
If, like me, you enjoy working for 25 minutes or so at time, then certain trees won’t grow in this time. I think it can be a little unreasonable to propose that people have to work 2 hours a day to ensure their tree grows.

There should be a special cancel button for exceptional occasions where you have to cancel it. Obviously to prevent this being abused and ruining the concept of the app, maybe there could be a limited number of times you can use it weekly etc?

Suggestions:

Allow the user to play their own music through the phone! I love study playlists but being unable to use my phone’s music capabilities can be frustrating. 

A “I’m still going” button. I’ve had some sessions where after my prescribed study period is over, yet I’m still focused and the whole process of setting up another session is enough to break immersion. A button which would allow the user to simply tap it at the end of the suggestion to keep going and it stores their time would be a fantastic addition.

That being said, the app is near flawless and for anyone looking for a worthwhile productivity app simply look no further than Forest.

title: Fun app for students
body:
I bought this app to use while I study for my university courses. It’s fun and easy to use, relatively straightforward to navigate. Surprisingly the concept of “killing” my tree has kept me motivated to stay off my phone!

However it’s not without problems. The whole idea is that by staying productive you earn points - which you can use to “buy” different tree types or background music, with the option to save up and spend your points on an actual, real life tree. I think the prices of tree types and such is set way too high, let alone the price of the real tree!

I also often forget to turn the app on, maybe you could add a feature to set daily notifications? If that’s already a feature I can’t seem to enable it... 

Finally, there’s the option to add friends and stay productive/off our phones together. However I feel the community aspect is less developed and finding and managing friends could be more straightforward.

title: Very effective tool for focus
body:
So, as an 'executive' (whatever that means), I'm quite organised/have good systems. That said, continually working with/against maladaptive emotional states (also have a therapist, lol) - worked with lots of pomodoro apps in the past - this is first one which actually works over the long term in respect of genuine lever against procrastination or distraction. And that's said as someone who has no particular love for trees. 

Clincher for me is that I don't want any dead trees on my plot. Reward mechanics work well too, re: gaining credits, buying new tree varieties - cute and pleasant. 

Secondily, other people who come in to interrupt for some reason recognise that I'm growing a tree and find it entirely reasonable that I can't stop - namely my wife. Unexpected effect, lol. 

I only use it for deep focus/long term projects (re: masters assignments; blog posts; reports) and not in day to day - this works for me as it allows me to really be unrelenting in not accepting interruptions and part of that is only using it when I know I can schedule some deep work (being the only type of work that I personally need help with focus and procrastination.) 

Well worth £1.99.

title: Great focus app
body:
Honestly one of the best tools I’ve ever used! Great for helping stay on track with revision! 

I often like to have some background noise while I’m working but the tv and radio are too distracting, first has a wide range of ambient sounds that you can listen to while you’re working. It also has a silent function for those who find quiet better for focusing.

The in app tracker for how long you’ve managed to stay on task is also very useful.  It provides a visual of how long you’ve stayed on track and also gives a sense of achievement when you see how many trees you’ve grown. 

It also has a label function and different trees for if you like to segment your tasks. This means you can easily see how long you’ve managed to focused on which areas and pinpoint which ones you’re not doing so well in.

title: Try harder!
body:
I like that I can assign tasks to time spent, that’s the best feature for me. 

My main peeve about this app is that when the time set is up it doesn’t make any sound on my iPhone and barely on my iPad. Isn’t a main feature supposed to be telling me when my time is up? How do I know when to take a break? So I often work few mins longer than time set so I have to check my phone often. Yes I’ve checked the sound effect in settings is on.

On iPad if I open another app while the timer is on it automatically stops and tells me to “try harder”. I use other apps on my iPad to work.

Update:
Response to developer- the setting on in the app is set to allow notifications as it is in iPhone settings too. Even when it isn’t on do not disturb no sounds is made to alert time complete.

title: Kick old habits
body:
After my a level mocks flopped due to my inability to focus (because of distractions) and lack of self discipline, I decided to look for something that would stop that. My friends suggested this app which I already had but never used and it has completely changed my level of productivity!
Growing trees is an incentive itself as well as working hard knowing that you can earn coins to buy trees etc which is definitely a great bonus. I’ve yet to see the results so hopefully in my upcoming tests I’ll see a great deal of change in my scores as I know I can achieve what I want if I revise.

Negative: The global stats are full of people who plant trees just because they want to without real purpose and so I can’t get the achievements of being in the top100. A bit pointless on my end tbh.

TLDR; definitely worth £1.99 as it can boost your productivity levels by a lot.

title: PLEASE LISTEN TO MY IMPROVEMENTS
body:
Okay, i love this app don’t get me wrong but i genuinely believe it could be made better by:
1) adding more tree/bush species (the ones you have are great but there needs to be a greater variety
2) It should be made that the better looking trees should be earned through studying a longer time. This will actually motivate people to work for longer and not quit because they want these newer, more unique trees 
3) your forest shouldn’t disappear each day but actually add to a collection of all the trees you’ve grown since using the app, this should also be customisable ie. be able to move the trees around 
4) i understand in point 3) that some people use the app to visualise time as trees per day so you could even just make two views, one with the trees you’ve grown today, yesterday etc as normal but then another view where you can see your forest accumulated over the time since using the app, i feel like this would allow you to be more appreciative of the time you’ve spent growing your forest rather than it disappearing day to day 
5) lastly, regarding that last point, you could also allow players to view their friends forests so that they can compare and compete with friends to see who can grow a bigger forest with the greatest variety of species etc i feel competition may be healthy in encouraging individuals to spend more time studying or just be nice for some inspiration even 

of course these are just thoughts of mine but i really do think they’ll make this app a lot better

title: Pomodoro but better
body:
I've been a fan of the pomodoro technique since I discovered it, but I've never quite managed to get it to stick. This simple little app changed all of that for me. It's essentially a simple gamifying of the pomodoro technique (in which you work on a task for a focussed burst, then have a short break, then repeat). This app plants a virtual tree in a virtual glade if you manage to leave your phone untouched for the amount of time you set. At the end of the day you can see how much time you've spent focussing based on how many trees you have in your glade. 
I don't know why visualising the time in this way has such a profound effect, but it does. I know I can't touch my phone, so I know I may as well get on with the task at hand. Even if you don't want to use it for work, but for down time, it's effective. Set it, and forget about your phone for an hour. Read a book, go for a walk. You'll have a lovely virtual tree to admire when you get back.

title: The incentives are really effective
body:
I've been using this app for 3 months now, and it's helped immensely with being able to study for exams.

title: The perfect solution to compulsive phone checking
body:
I have tried every cure for phone addiction in the book. I have tried deleting Facebook and Twitter from my phone, I have tried downloading an app that bans me from using those sites, I have even tried good old self control, but none of it has helped. This is a big problem for me, because I have an OCD so websites that encourage compulsive behaviour are a huge problem if I'm already not doing well.

This app is the perfect solution! It's a carrot, rather than stick, approach, and it really works. The first three days of barely using my phone were really difficult, but in the first three days there are lots of rewards to help get you through. As you get better at doing without your phone, the rewards get harder and harder to achieve, which means they are always set to the appropriate level for your ability. 

It's generally a very intelligently designed app. It has extremely cute graphics, and the the set up is that the more time you commit to growing a tree, the more beautiful the tree will be. 30 minutes without your phone wins you a tree, 2 hours wins you a tree with adorable birds in it. So you're constantly incentivised to push yourself to loosen the phone's grip on you. Also, you'll be amazed how much you don't want to kill that tree! 

Try it, it works. It's completely changed my relationship with my phone, and made me feel much happier and in control.

title: Brilliantly effective and simple
body:
In my experience there are two types of workers. Those who find it hard to concentrate, and those who forget to take breaks. This app helps with both. Set a time you want to work for and get your head down. Don't leave the app or your tree will die. When the timer goes off have a 5-10 min break and do some of the things that wanted to distract you while you were working. I love it.
One potential improvement would be something like a repeating work/rest timer along the lines of Pomodoro. E.g 25 mins work, 5 mins rest, repeat 4 times then 30 mins rest.

title: Good, slightly upset
body:
Update 2: Good, slightly upset

Ok so I admit it was harsh to give this app 2 stars over my unpreparedness but I'd love to see a feature that allows you to use your calculator, or as said below have a proper scientific calculator integrated into the app, I would pay in app purchases for that :) or even a regular calculator would be awesome!

Update: unhappy

Why can't I use my calculator? I need it for physics why on earth not? I'm not a genius or work out 40/(0.7x0.5) with no mistake without a calculator. I'm only in year 9, I'm not the best at math and you don't have a lot of time in the exam! I do not have my calculator on me right now I left it at home so now the app is pretty much unusable for Physics and Math. Which are two very important subjects for me. Not happy at all. Should at least let you use your notification centre where the calculator is or if that doesn't work have a proper calculator integrated into the app (the proper scientific one) I will happily pay for that. Still really mad tho.

It was quite a good experience the first time I tried it, it helped me keep somewhat focused and I have a really bad habit of going on my phone when I worked. This does what it says and it used the words cute when u want to give up (that got me to focus) but I found myself accidentally pressing plant when I don't have any time to concentrate for 15 more minutes and having to reinstall the app. Now I would happily stay up another 15 minutes but it's 2am and I can't it's way past when I'm supposed to sleep anyway, there must be a cheaper way than 60 coins to get rid of a piece of weed. Already really unhappy that I have to reinstall the app with such slow internet speed but I'll give it another shot 👍🏼. 

Also I would like to please see more features. Maybe more things to buy or a lake or animals or benches would work well or people. I feel like it's a little too plain especially for a paid app. Also more features would help keep me motivated. Please add more features!

But atleast the app does what it says and does it quite well

title: Brilliant productivity app - download!
body:
Simple and effective! 

Clean, pleasing on the eye user interface plus useful concept to manage your time better. 

Set your time interval duration, select plant a tree and begin your task without touching your phone. If you do, you will kill your tree! This gives a playful sense of genuinely caring about a virtual growing organism which powers (me anyway) to keep strong. Once the time is up - check the app to see your new tree planted in your daily forest. 

Despite other saying otherwise, being able to work with your phone is handy for me. For example I tend to use my phone for emails, editing pics, tracking finance expenditure, using Evernote etc and this function enables me to do so. 

Ultimately at the end of the day it is a tiny bit of the placebo effect of shaping our willpower! 

Extremely happy with the update - an adjustable timer and ability to unlock able tree varieties. 

Don't hesitate to download it and make it a staple part of your everyday routine!

Updated 08/03/16:

Please enable us to personalise more options in the categories of what we did / timed ourselves on. I'd love to be able to edit this and add my own in. Also interchangeable icons for categories would be good. And perhaps different colours to help differentiate! Re: when your tree has grown and you click the pen icon.

title: It could be better
body:
This app is an aid for iPhone addicts (like me). However, it would be more useful if the timer is more flexible. Currently, the timer is set at 30-minute intervals, meaning that you can set timers for 30 minutes, one hour, 1.5 hours and so on. But I like to work in 45-minute intervals, so I am tempted to keep checking the time, which becomes distracting.

The app could also add some features that would make it more fun/addictive. For example, have more tree variety (e.g. Cherry blossom for spring, maple for autumn, fully decorated Christmas tree for winter, surprise seeds), other smaller plants for shorter time intervals (e.g. Flowers or bushes), different terrains, save-a-tree potion to revive a dying tree etc.
